_comment: Canonical behavior table for the AI preference gate, executed by BOTH sides:
The client reads its copy from app/frontend/tests/fixtures/ai_pref_gate_cases.js,
which a spec here asserts is structurally identical to this file. Editing one
side's behavior without the other now fails that side's own suite.
'prefs' is the literal settings['preferences'] hash; an omitted key means the
preference was never written (undefined in JS, nil in Ruby).

cases.name: absent master grandfathers a gated feature
absent master grandfathers an ungated feature
explicit null master grandfathers
empty-string master denies a gated feature
empty-string master denies an UNGATED feature too
empty-string master denies even with the child opted in
unrecognized master denies a gated feature
unrecognized master denies an UNGATED feature too
object master denies
ascii-space master denies
non-breaking-space master denies (Ruby strip and JS trim disagree here; with no blank test there is no divergence)
NUL master denies (the same disagreement in the other direction)
boolean false master denies
string false master denies
numeric 0 master denies
string 0 master denies
numeric 0 master denies an ungated feature too
explicit false master beats an opted-in child
true master plus true child allows
string true master plus string true child allows
string 1 master plus numeric 1 child allows
numeric 1 master plus string 1 child allows
true master allows an ungated feature without any child key
true master with absent child denies (incomplete opt-in)
true master with empty-string child denies
true master with unrecognized child denies
true master with false child denies
true master with numeric 0 child denies
true master with null child denies
one gated feature opted in does not enable a sibling
